headline: Oil is over $100. Seven countries won't pump more.
summary: Seven oil exporters, Saudi Arabia and Russia among them, agreed on Sunday to hold production steady in November. The Iran war has pushed Brent crude above $100 a barrel and US diesel to record highs. The G7 is releasing 100 million barrels from its reserves instead, diesel first, within 20 days. The seven meet again on November 1.
cover_answer: Seven countries. Today they chose: no more.
table_question: If you had what everyone needed, would you sell more or hold back?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Oil comes out of the ground in a few countries, and today seven of them agreed to pump the same amount next month, not more. Oil is what trucks and tractors run on, and right now it costs a lot, like a juice box jumping from one dollar to two. Some big countries are opening their stored-up barrels to help. The grown-ups are on it.
5-7.why: A juice box doubling in price is a thing a six-year-old can feel. A barrel at $100 is not.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what they can hold, so the script turns a $100 barrel into a juice box that doubled in price and oil into what trucks and tractors drink. The war stays a word, not a picture: Cantor found this age fears what it can see. Expect "will we run out?" Say no, the stored barrels are being opened now.

8-12.script: A war with Iran cut the flow of oil, so there's less of it and the price passed $100 a barrel. Seven big producers could pump more, like turning up a thermostat, and today they left the dial alone. The G7 is opening its stockpile instead, 100 million barrels, diesel first.
8-12.why: Supply, price and a dial someone chose not to turn.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script runs the chain in order: a war cuts supply, less oil means a higher price, seven countries hold the dial, and the G7 reaches for its stockpile. The thermostat is a mechanism they already know. Expect "why won't they just pump more?" Honest answer: the articles don't say.

13-17.script: If seven countries could cut fuel prices by pumping more and don't, is that their right or a squeeze? Oil is over $100 in the Iran war, and today Saudi Arabia, Russia and five others held output flat. Second: the G7 answers with 100 million barrels. Then what?
13-17.why: Sovereignty or leverage, and a stockpile with a bottom.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a country may sell as much of its own oil as it likes, and seven of them choosing not to leaves farmers and truckers paying record prices. The script asks them to argue it both ways, which Kuhn says is how arguing gets learned. Expect "so who's the bad guy?" Say the article names none.

5-7.q: Why does fuel cost so much?
5-7.a: There's a war where a lot of oil comes from, so less of it is getting out. Less to go round means a higher price.

8-12.a: Nobody alone. Seven big producers meet and set how much they pump, and today they agreed on no change.

8-12.q: Why don't they just pump more?
8-12.a: They could. Today they chose not to, and they meet again on November 1 to decide about December.

13-17.q: Why is diesel the first thing released?
13-17.a: Diesel hit record highs in the US, and farmers and truckers run on it. The G7 promises diesel first, within 20 days.

13-17.q: Does holding steady mean prices stay high?
13-17.a: No new supply from those seven. Only the G7 barrels are coming, over four months.
